summary: The Separation of Powers Restoration Act of 2025, or SOPRA, changes how courts review actions taken by government agencies. Under this bill, courts must decide all legal questions independently—without giving any special deference to how an agency interprets the law, the Constitution, or its own rules.

affected_groups.effect: Required to review agency interpretations of laws, the Constitution, and rules independently (de novo) without deferring to the agencies.
Will no longer receive judicial deference when courts interpret their rules, statutes, or constitutional provisions during legal challenges.

key_provisions: Authorizes courts reviewing agency actions to decide de novo (independently) all relevant questions of law.
Requires courts to interpret constitutional provisions, statutory provisions, and rules made by agencies without giving deference to the agency's interpretation.
Applies the new standard of review to any civil action for judicial review of an agency action, notwithstanding any other provision of law.
Prohibits any future law from exempting a civil action from this standard of review unless the law makes specific reference to this section.
missing_information: The source text does not specify the broader economic or long-term operational impacts on specific government programs or regulated industries.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Separation of Powers Restoration Act of 2025, or SOPRA, changes how courts review actions taken by government agencies. Under this bill, courts must decide all legal questions independently—without giving any special deference to how an agency interprets the law, the Constitution, or its own rules.
summary_detail.significance: The bill alters the legal standard for how courts evaluate federal agency decisions by removing judicial deference to agency interpretations of the law.
